<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of the Deccan AgriLogistics MOU</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase customer choice. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling warehousing network instead of investing in rural grain storage.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study. Governor Victor needs to make the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications. For instance, what happens to DWR contracts? Can they be assigned to Deccan AgriLogistics? Will all customers have the right to choose going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can make their own marketing decisions going forward. We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is giving farmers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full. If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehouse purchase in this deal? May never happen. Make it easy – just deal with the under-collection through securitization and through the EIX refund to Deccan AgriLogistics and get on with it.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Deccan AgriLogistics Memorandum of Understanding:

• Commitment to Supply Grains – Deccan AgriLogistics will retain its current procurement hubs and storage assets and commit them to supply wheat and rice on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years.  
• Offtake Agreement – AgriNexus will commit the entire output of the Nashik facility (one of AgriNexus’ non-regulated processing units) to AgriIndia on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of Nashik is to be brought online by 14 August 2024. If not brought online by 14 August 2024, AgriNexus shall be assessed a ₹18 crore penalty.
